places.name: Göreme Open-Air Museum
places.ai_summary: A UNESCO World Heritage site, the Göreme Open-Air Museum features ancient rock-cut churches adorned with stunning frescoes.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited early morning to avoid crowds.

places.place_tip: Hire a guide to learn about the history of the frescoes.

Göreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia
Göreme is a town in the Cappadocia region of central Turkey. Just east of town is the Göreme Open Air Museum, with cave churches and frescoes from the 10th to 12th centuries. Southwest is Uçhisar Castle, a fortification carved into a large rock, with panoramic views from the top. To the north, the landscape at Paşabağ Valley is known for Cappadocia’s “fairy chimneys,” cone-shaped rock formations.
Göreme National Park is a national park in central Turkey. It occupies an area of nearly 100 km2 (39 sq mi) and is located in Nevşehir Province. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985 under the name Goreme National Park and the Rock Sites of Cappadocia. The park features a rocky, water- and wind-eroded landscape with a network of ancient, interconnecting underground settlements.

In a spectacular landscape, entirely sculpted by erosion, the Göreme valley and its surroundings contain rock-hewn sanctuaries that provide unique evidence of Byzantine art in the post-Iconoclastic period. Dwellings, troglodyte villages and underground towns – the remains of a traditional human habitat dating back to the 4th century – can also be seen there.

places.name: Hot Air Balloon Ride
places.ai_summary: Experience the breathtaking landscapes of Cappadocia from above with a hot air balloon ride, a must-do activity in the region.

opening_hours.notes: Flights are weather-dependent.

places.place_tip: Book in advance to secure a spot during peak season.

places.name: Uçhisar Castle
places.ai_summary: Uçhisar Castle is a natural rock formation offering panoramic views of Cappadocia's fairy chimneys and valleys.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited at sunset for stunning views.

places.place_tip: Wear comfortable shoes for the climb to the top.

places.name: Devrent Valley
places.ai_summary: Also known as Imagination Valley, Devrent Valley is famous for its unique rock formations that resemble various animal shapes.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the late afternoon for the best light for photography.

places.place_tip: Let your imagination run wild with the rock formations' shapes.

places.name: Pasabag
places.ai_summary: Pasabag, also known as Monks Valley, is renowned for its mushroom-shaped fairy chimneys and historical hermit caves.

opening_hours.notes: The valley is best explored on foot.

places.place_tip: Visit the Zelve Open-Air Museum nearby for more fairy chimneys.

places.name: Kaymakli Underground City
places.ai_summary: Kaymakli Underground City is one of the largest and deepest underground cities in Cappadocia, used historically as a refuge during invasions.

opening_hours.notes: The underground city can be chilly, so dress warmly.

places.place_tip: Take a guided tour to learn about the city's history and structure.

places.name: Derinkuyu Underground City
places.ai_summary: Derinkuyu Underground City is the deepest of the Cappadocia underground cities, extending to about 60 meters deep.

opening_hours.notes: Wear comfortable shoes as the floors can be uneven.

places.place_tip: Visit the wine cellars and learn about ancient wine-making techniques.

places.name: Love Valley
places.ai_summary: Love Valley is famous for its unique rock formations and is a popular spot for hiking and photography.

opening_hours.notes: The valley is best explored on foot.

places.place_tip: Bring plenty of water and wear sturdy shoes.

places.name: Pigeon Valley
places.ai_summary: Pigeon Valley is known for its dovecotes carved into the rocks and is a great place for a scenic hike.

opening_hours.notes: Watch your step as the trails can be rocky.

places.place_tip: Early morning is the best time to visit for birdwatching.

places.name: Ortahisar Castle
places.ai_summary: Ortahisar Castle is a natural rock citadel with a rich history, offering stunning views of the surrounding area.

opening_hours.notes: The castle is best visited in the late afternoon.

places.place_tip: Explore the surrounding village for a glimpse of local life.

places.name: Avanos
places.ai_summary: Avanos is a town famous for its pottery and the Kızılırmak River, offering a unique blend of culture and nature.

opening_hours.notes: Don't miss the pottery workshops and the river walk.

places.place_tip: Try your hand at pottery-making in one of the local workshops.

places.name: Zelve Open-Air Museum
places.ai_summary: Zelve Open-Air Museum is an ancient cave town and a UNESCO World Heritage site, showcasing the region's unique rock-cut architecture.

opening_hours.notes: The museum is less crowded in the late afternoon.

places.place_tip: Explore the nearby valleys for more stunning landscapes.

places.name: Rose Valley
places.ai_summary: Rose Valley is known for its beautiful pink-hued rock formations and is a popular spot for hiking and photography.

opening_hours.notes: The valley is best explored on foot.

places.place_tip: Visit the valley during sunset for a magical experience.

places.name: Red Valley
places.ai_summary: Red Valley is famous for its stunning red rock formations and is a great place for hiking and watching the sunset.

opening_hours.notes: The valley is best explored on foot.

places.place_tip: Bring a camera to capture the stunning landscapes.

places.name: Çavuşin Village
places.ai_summary: Çavuşin Village is an old Greek village with traditional stone houses and a beautiful church, offering a glimpse into the region's history.

opening_hours.notes: The village is quiet and less crowded, perfect for a peaceful visit.

places.place_tip: Explore the surrounding areas for more rock-cut churches.

places.name: Ihlara Valley
places.ai_summary: Ihlara Valley is a beautiful gorge with a river running through it, known for its hiking trails and rock-cut churches.

opening_hours.notes: The valley is cooler than the surrounding areas, making it a great escape in summer.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the rock-cut churches with frescoes along the hiking trail.

places.name: Mustafapaşa
places.ai_summary: Mustafapaşa is an old Greek village with well-preserved stone houses and a rich history, located near Cappadocia.

opening_hours.notes: The village is quiet and less touristy, offering an authentic experience.

places.place_tip: Explore the old churches and enjoy the village's tranquility.

places.name: Sobesos Ancient City
places.ai_summary: Sobesos Ancient City is an archaeological site with well-preserved ruins, including a bathhouse and a basilica.

opening_hours.notes: The site is less crowded in the early morning.

places.place_tip: Bring a hat and water, as there is little shade at the site.

places.name: Fairy Chimneys
places.ai_summary: The Fairy Chimneys are unique rock formations in Cappadocia, resembling chimneys, and are a popular subject for photography.

opening_hours.notes: The best light for photography is during the golden hour.

places.place_tip: Visit the nearby valleys for more stunning fairy chimneys.

places.name: Horseback Riding Tours
places.ai_summary: Explore the beautiful landscapes of Cappadocia on horseback, an unforgettable way to experience the region's natural beauty.

opening_hours.notes: Advance booking is recommended, especially during peak season.

places.place_tip: Choose a tour that includes a visit to the hidden valleys.
